scope.summary: Build the Blender/UE round-trip verification harness per Section 13.26 (REQ-044): headless Blender scripts and UE-import checks that verify morphs, skeleton, correctives, scale, and orientation survive each export lane — with the Daz-bridge pain list encoded verbatim as named acceptance tests (morph selection stability, geograft-morph survival, bone rotation bugs, A-pose reference mismatch, 0.01 scale issues).
acceptance_criteria: The Blender leg runs headless (blender --background --python) importing an export and asserting: all selected morphs present with correct names/ranges, skeleton hierarchy and bone count intact, driver-sidecar generators apply cleanly, world scale exact, up-axis correct.
The UE leg validates via UE-import checks (commandlet or structural FBX/glTF assertions where a UE install is absent) covering skeleton compatibility, morph presence, and unit scale.

The Daz-bridge pain list maps to named tests: morph_selection_stable, geograft_morphs_survive_single_mesh_lane, bone_rotation_correct_ue5, a_pose_reference_mismatch_fixed, no_scale_001_import_bug — each must pass on its owning lane.
Toolchain absence (no Blender/UE in the environment) records a typed SKIPPED-with-reason result, never a silent pass; CI runners with tooling run the full harness.
Harness results integrate into EXPORT_BODY_VALID as round-trip check entries.
scope.risk_if_missed: Export correctness is asserted, never proven in the actual consumers — and BodyKit re-ships the precise catalog of bridge failures that drove the operator off Daz in the first place.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend/solver scope: behavior is observable via TraceProjection, typed TAILOR_BODY_* receipts, and the 13.12 capture APIs; operator/model GUI exposure rides the BodyKit panes (13.27) and is validated there.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Emits/extends the TAILOR_BODY_* KernelEventType family on the EventLedger per Section 13.16 (extends the 13.14 canonical list).
internal_diagnostics ships with WP-KERNEL-012; wire the open diagnostic-event API for this behavior in the WP-KERNEL-016 retrofit.
Palmistry external watcher ships with WP-KERNEL-012/016; long generation/bake/export runs get child-stall watch coverage in the retrofit.

risks: Broad MT scope can hide multiple review targets.
Markdown MT lists may disagree with packet-declared active/next MT truth.
Receipt routing may target an old MT if contract identity is omitted.
minimum_controls: Exactly one primary proof target per MT unless the packet records why not.
MT identity must be stable and referenced by receipt correlation.
Generated projection drift must not wake Coder or Validator by itself.
